findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Bound the register-owned branch: state an expected cut-vs-register split (or cap on newly-registered owned entries) and add a check that any owned entry for these paths carries a rationale matching the 'test-only control / protocol constant' category, so register-owned cannot rubber-stamp reads that should be cut to the seam.
evidence: Outcome: 'or (b) REGISTERED as an owned, non-legacy entry with an exact path+symbol+rationale for genuine test-only controls and protocol constants'
Held-out test asserts only: LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS 'contains zero entries whose path is one of the listed files' and no finding string contains the paths
'genuine test-only controls and protocol constants' is a subjective classification with no proving command
findings.finding: The 'register-owned (non-legacy)' escape branch (outcome (b)) is not bounded or verified: the held-out test only asserts zero LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS entries for these paths, so an executor could reclassify all 18 reads as 'owned' non-legacy exceptions and pass the gate without cutting any read to a seam. Nothing measures that a registered entry is a 'genuine test-only control or protocol constant.'
scenarios: Executor registers ambient reads as owned rather than cutting to seam, defeating the RP-04 intent while the held-out test still passes
findings.suggested_fix: Enumerate in the plan which of the 18 reads are expected to be cut vs registered (with the specific symbol+rationale per registered entry), and assert that count in the held-out test.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion or held-out assertion that bounds/justifies the register-owned branch — e.g. enumerate which of the 18 reads are cut-to-seam vs owned, and assert each owned entry's rationale matches a genuine test-only-control/protocol-constant pattern — so the gate cannot be satisfied by relabeling ambient reads as owned.
evidence: Outcome: '(b) REGISTERED as an owned, non-legacy entry with an exact path+symbol+rationale for genuine test-only controls and protocol constants'
Testing: held-out test asserts 'LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS contains zero entries whose path is one of the listed files' — it does not constrain how many reads are reclassified as owned vs genuinely cut
The held-out test is a structural AST/exception-table check; without a bound on register-owned it can be satisfied by relabeling rather than cutting
findings.finding: The register-owned branch (option b) lets a below-seam read be moved from LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS to an 'owned, non-legacy' entry, and the held-out test only verifies that no LEGACY entry and no path-glob remain for these paths — it does not verify that a registered-owned read is genuinely a test-only control or protocol constant. A read could be relabeled to owned to make the gate pass without any real cut-to-seam, and the suite would still go green.
findings.location: Outcome / Testing (RED->GREEN) — 'REGISTERED as an owned, non-legacy entry' and the held-out test description

findings.checklist_item: State the explicit rule that decides cut-to-seam vs register-owned for each read (e.g. 'value derives from a _config_schema.py section -> cut through the snapshot; test-harness/ops runtime knob or protocol constant read at call time -> register with rationale; subprocess-env propagation -> out of scope / not a config read'), and apply it to each of the 18 reads.
evidence: Outcome: 'is either (a) CUT to compose through the approved seam ... or (b) REGISTERED as an owned, non-legacy entry ... for genuine test-only controls and protocol constants'

The 10 files mix genuine config (load_config().sync.push in _store/push.py:63, load_config().ensure in _store/ensures.py:245, load_config().jira.project in _store/project_ensures.py:69) with runtime/test/ops knobs (REBAR_HLC_NOW in _store/hlc.py:71, REBAR_LOCK_RETRIES in _store/lock.py:419 which carries an in-code comment on why it is a deliberate literal below-seam read, REBAR_ALLOW_ENV_REIDENTIFY in _store/env_identity.py:109, REBAR_SNAPSHOT_STALL_* in _snapshot/git_fetch.py, REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR in _snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:119) and pure subprocess-env propagation ({**os.environ, ...} in _store/push.py:207/264, _snapshot/git_fetch.py:263, _snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:354/381)
findings.finding: The plan gives no decision rule for classifying each below-seam read as cut-to-seam (a) vs register-owned (b); the two options are named but the criterion that separates them is left implicit, so the implementer must guess which of the 18 reads are 'genuine test-only controls / protocol constants' vs threadable config.
scenarios: Implementer cuts a harness/ops knob (e.g. REBAR_HLC_NOW) into the snapshot that should have been registered, breaking the skewed-clock test harness
Implementer registers a genuine config read (sync.push) as owned instead of cutting it, defeating RP-04's seam intent while still turning the gate green

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State where an approved fingerprint delta is recorded (e.g. an updated fixture/snapshot file committed with the change and referenced in the PR) and the default that ANY unrecorded fingerprint change fails the criterion.
evidence: 'redacted operation-snapshot fingerprints / provider-neutral outcomes are unchanged except recorded, justified deltas'
No location named for where a delta is recorded or who justifies it
findings.finding: The 'recorded, justified deltas' allowance for redacted operation-snapshot fingerprints has no stated recording location or approver, leaving the fingerprint-equality criterion partially defaultable.
scenarios: A behavioral fingerprint changes during the cutover and the executor must decide whether it is an approved delta
findings.suggested_fix: Add: 'Any fingerprint delta must be captured as an updated committed snapshot fixture with a one-line rationale in the PR; unrecorded deltas fail the suite.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the consumers/callers OUTSIDE _io/_snapshot/_store that must be updated when below-seam function signatures change to accept threaded config (e.g. _lib_reads.py, _io/_cli.py, _io/__init__.py, _commands/init.py, _commands/fsck_tracker_health.py), or state that cut-to-seam will be done without altering any public signature.
evidence: Plan step 1: 'for cut-to-seam, thread the value from the composition seam rather than reading ambient os.environ/os.getenv/load_config below it.'
External callers exist: src/rebar/_lib_reads.py:109 'return import_ndjson.import_tickets(source, dry_run=dry_run, repo_root=repo_root)'
src/rebar/_io/_cli.py:15 and src/rebar/_io/__init__.py:20 import import_tickets
src/rebar/_commands/init.py:27 'from rebar._store.env_identity import mint_env_id_guarded'; src/rebar/_commands/fsck_tracker_health.py:64 calls env_identity.read_env_id / divergence_report
The plan lists only the 10 below-seam files and names no callers/consumers of their public entrypoints.
findings.finding: The plan's cut-to-seam strategy threads config values into below-seam functions (changing their signatures to accept a composed value instead of reading ambient os.environ), but it enumerates no consumers/callers of those functions that live outside the _io/_snapshot/_store directories and would need updating to pass the threaded value.
findings.location: Plan step 1 / Outcome ('thread the value from the composition seam rather than reading ambient os.environ/os.getenv/load_config below it')
scenarios: Threading a snapshot/config value up through import_tickets or env_identity functions changes their signatures, breaking callers in _lib_reads.py, _io/_cli.py, _io/__init__.py, _commands/init.py, and _commands/fsck_tracker_health.py that are not listed in the plan.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Ground the per-file premise: cite where 29a9's LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS is enumerated (or attach the current entry list) confirming EACH of the 10 listed files has at least one entry to remove, and that the total for these paths is the claimed 18 — so the held-out per-file assertion cannot pass vacuously for a file with no pre-existing entry.
evidence: Plan: 'Slice C1 (ticket 29a9-3cf7-3ded-42d8) recorded 18 below-seam ambient config/credential reads in the store / snapshot / io subsystem (_store, _snapshot, _io) ... as entries in scripts/config_ownership_exceptions.LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS.'
show_ticket(29a9) Outcome: 'An initial legacy-exception set enumerates current below-seam reads' — does not enumerate the 18 nor map them to the 10 named files.

config_ownership_exceptions.py / LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS are prereq-created (verified via 29a9 file_impact + 075b manifest pins), so the per-file entry mapping cannot be read directly and is not established in retrievable prereq text.
The held-out test's per-file assertion passes vacuously for any listed file that had no entry to begin with.
findings.finding: The quantitative premise '18 below-seam ambient config/credential reads ... recorded ... as entries in LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS' and the implicit assumption that EACH of the 10 listed files currently carries a removable LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS entry are load-bearing (they define the RED state and what the held-out test removes), but are not affirmatively confirmed by the cited prerequisite (29a9). 29a9's Outcome states only that 'an initial legacy-exception set enumerates current below-seam reads' — it neither enumerates the 18 nor confirms every one of these 10 files has an entry. A file with zero pre-existing entries would make step 2 ('remove the corresponding entries for these files') and the held-out 'zero entries whose path is one of the listed files' assertion vacuously pass while leaving an un-cut below-seam read undetected for that file.
findings.location: Context/Problem ('18 below-seam ambient config/credential reads ... as entries in LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS') and Testing ('config_ownership_exceptions.LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS contains zero entries whose path is one of the listed files')
scenarios: A listed file (e.g., import_ndjson.py) has an ambient read that the C1 gate classified as an approved owner rather than a legacy exception; the plan's RED premise is false for that file and step 2 removes nothing, yet AC-2 and the held-out test report green.
The '18' count drifts (some reads already cut by an earlier slice) so the plan's scope no longer matches the real legacy-exception set.

findings.checklist_item: For each read the plan intends to CUT, confirm the value is a config-schema section the snapshot already carries (or record the schema addition required); explicitly exclude per-tick/per-attempt runtime knobs (REBAR_HLC_NOW, REBAR_LOCK_RETRIES) and subprocess-env propagation from cut-to-seam and route them to register-owned instead.
evidence: _operation_config.py:132-138 build() validates only values whose leaves are JSON primitives keyed by section/key; the snapshot carries no runtime clock/retry knob unless added to _config_schema.py
hlc.py:67-77 physical_now() reads REBAR_HLC_NOW on every call (the skewed-clock harness injection point), not once per operation
lock.py:411-426 write_path_retries() reads REBAR_LOCK_RETRIES at call time and its docstring explicitly documents it as a deliberate literal below-seam read for gen_env_registry visibility
findings.finding: The plan asserts cut-to-seam threads the value 'from the composition seam' but does not establish that the OperationSnapshot (a frozen, per-operation, config-schema-only object composed above the store) can actually supply the values read by per-tick / per-attempt leaf callers such as physical_now() (REBAR_HLC_NOW, read on every next_tick) or write_path_retries() (REBAR_LOCK_RETRIES). These are neither config-schema fields nor once-per-operation values, so 'thread from the snapshot' may be mechanically infeasible for them without a schema change the plan does not mention.
findings.location: Plan step 1 ('thread the value from the composition seam')
scenarios: Implementer attempts to thread REBAR_HLC_NOW through compose_operation_snapshot and finds the snapshot is composed above the store and frozen per-operation, unable to carry a per-tick harness override
A cut that plumbs a per-operation snapshot into a leaf helper changes its call signature across the whole store, expanding blast radius well beyond the 10 files

findings.checklist_item: Add a one- or two-sentence positive rationale for the chosen approach — why genuine config is cut through the OperationSnapshot while call-time ops/test knobs (kept as literal reads for gen_env_registry visibility) are the correct register-owned cases.
evidence: Neither Outcome nor Plan states why register-owned is appropriate for the harness/ops knobs (the in-code comment at lock.py:417-418 supplies the real rationale: literal below-seam reads keep gen_env_registry documentation intact) — the plan does not surface this reasoning
ABSENCE: no sentence in the plan explains the fitness of the two-path approach for these specific read species
findings.finding: The plan states no positive rationale for WHY the chosen dual mechanism (cut-through-snapshot for some reads, register-owned for others) is the right fit for THIS subsystem — in particular why leaf-level ops/test knobs are best left below the seam as owned entries rather than lifted. Without the rationale the implementer cannot tell whether a register-owned choice is a principled decision or a shortcut to green the gate.
scenarios: Reviewer or implementer cannot distinguish a justified register-owned entry from one added merely to silence the gate
